ai.description: This lizard reaches 10–12 cm. It is brown with a pale lateral stripe. Key features include a smooth-scaled, flattened back and a distinctively sharp, ridge-like crest along the dorsal midline.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cristidorsa planidorsata* is best distinguished by the absence of a distinct vertebral crest, featuring instead a smooth, flattened back that lacks the prominent spines found in related mountain lizards.
ai.habitat: *Cristidorsa planidorsata* inhabits the high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Smooth-Scaled Mountain Lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among rocky outcrops and vegetation during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cristidorsa planidorsata* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cristidorsa planidorsata* is endemic to the high-altitude evergreen forests of the Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya, India, typically occurring above 1,000 meters.
